names.official: Personal income tax on dependent activity and functional benefits
names.native: Daň z příjmů fyzických osob ze závislé činnosti a funkčních požitků

taxes.base: Wages and salaries of employees.

rate.headline: 15% · 23% above CZK 1.76 million
details: Gross annual income up to CZK 1,762,812 (36 times the average monthly salary) is taxed at 15%; the excess at 23% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: The largest direct tax on persons: CZK 238 billion in 2024.

names.official: Personal income tax on independent gainful activity
names.native: Daň z příjmů fyzických osob ze samostatné výdělečné činnosti

taxes.base: Income of the self-employed.

rate.headline: Same 15% and 23% rates
details: As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: CZK 27.7 billion in 2024, up from CZK 21.9 billion.

names.official: Personal income tax on capital income
names.native: Daň z příjmů fyzických osob z kapitálových výnosů

taxes.base: Dividends, interest and other capital income, including income taxed by final withholding at source.

rate.headline: 15% withholding on Czech dividends and interest
details: Income already taxed by final withholding tax at source (for example dividends or interest from bonds of Czech companies) is excluded from the progressive scale; a 15% rate also applies to selected foreign investment income (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: CZK 46.6 billion in 2024.

names.official: Corporate income tax
names.native: Daň z příjmů právnických osob

taxes.base: Profit of companies and other legal persons.

rate.headline: 21% in 2024 and 2025 (19% before)
details: The standard CIT rate is 19%, raised to 21% in 2024 and 2025 (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: Revenue grew 14% in 2024 with the rate increase.

names.official: Tax on excess profits (windfall tax) and the top-up tax
names.native: Daň z nadměrných příjmů; dorovnávací daň

taxes.base: Excess profits of large banks and energy-sector companies in 2023–2025, and the top-up tax on large multinational groups.
taxes.payer: Large banks, energy companies and multinational groups.

rate.headline: 60% surcharge on excess profit (windfall tax)
details: In 2023 through 2025 a 60% CIT surcharge applies on top of the standard CIT, so the total on excess profits is 81% in 2024 and 2025 (PwC).
The top-up tax (CZK 1.0 billion) is a new line in 2024.
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: The windfall tax brought in CZK 40 billion in 2024, about 6% of all income taxes.

names.official: Employers’ contributions: pension, sickness, employment policy, accident and public health insurance
names.native: Pojistné placené zaměstnavateli

taxes.base: Gross pay. Pension insurance CZK 481 billion, health insurance CZK 205 billion, sickness insurance CZK 47 billion, employment policy CZK 27 billion, accident insurance CZK 12 billion, voluntary CZK 0.03 billion.

rate.headline: Set by the social and health insurance laws
details: The rates are not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: About three-fifths of all social contributions.

names.official: Employees’ contributions: pension, sickness and public health insurance
names.native: Pojistné placené zaměstnanci

taxes.base: Gross pay. Pension insurance CZK 145 billion, health insurance CZK 103 billion, sickness insurance CZK 13 billion (a new line in 2024).

rate.headline: Set by the social and health insurance laws
details: The rates are not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: Employees’ sickness insurance appears as a new line in 2024.

names.official: Contributions of the self-employed and voluntary contributions
names.native: Pojistné osob samostatně výdělečně činných; dobrovolné pojistné

taxes.base: Pension insurance CZK 42.8 billion, public health insurance CZK 36.2 billion and employment policy CZK 1.8 billion paid by the self-employed, and voluntary contributions of CZK 0.7 billion.
taxes.payer: Self-employed people and voluntarily insured persons.

rate.headline: Set by the social and health insurance laws

instruments.explanation: Five lines.

names.official: Public health insurance paid by the government for the non-employed
names.native: Pojistné na veřejné zdravotní pojištění placené vládou za nezaměstnané
names.common: Health insurance paid by the State for the non-employed

taxes.base: People insured by the State (children, pensioners and others who have no employer).
taxes.payer: The government, on behalf of the insured.

rate.headline: A fixed monthly amount per insured person
details: The List labels it "Public health insurance premium paid by the government for the unemployed". The monthly amount is not itemised in the list.

instruments.explanation: The statisticians count it as a contribution of households financed by a government transfer. It is a flow inside government; it is included here because the list includes it.

names.official: Value added tax
names.native: Daň z přidané hodnoty

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Czechia and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 21% standard; 12% reduced
details: 21% generally; 12% on groceries (except most drinks), medicines, tap water, hotel accommodation, admission to cultural and sports events, catering, heat and cold (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: The largest consumption tax: CZK 587 billion.

names.official: Customs duties
names.native: Clo

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

instruments.explanation: Collected for the EU budget.

names.official: Excise duty on mineral oils
names.native: Spotřební daň z minerálních olejů

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel and other mineral oils, by quantity. The list gives two lines: CZK 52.7 billion on goods from outside the EU and CZK 39.7 billion on the rest.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Per 1,000 litres, fixed by the Excise Duty Act

instruments.explanation: The biggest excise.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D2122C C01, D214A C01

names.official: Excise duty on tobacco
names.native: Spotřební daň z tabáku

taxes.base: Cigarettes and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Fixed by the Excise Duty Act

instruments.explanation: CZK 59.6 billion in 2024, up 13%.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D2122C C05, D214A C05

names.official: Excise duty on spirits, beer and wine
names.native: Spotřební daň z lihu, piva a vína

taxes.base: Spirits, beer and wine; six lines in the list.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre of product or pure alcohol

instruments.explanation: CZK 14.3 billion in 2024.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D2122C C02 to C04, D214A C02 to C04

names.official: Taxes on electricity, natural gas and solid fuels
names.native: Daň z elektřiny, zemního plynu a pevných paliv
names.common: Electricity, gas and solid fuel taxes

taxes.base: Electricity (CZK 1.5 billion), natural gas (CZK 1.6 billion) and solid fuels (CZK 0.3 billion).
taxes.payer: Suppliers; passed on in the price.

instruments.explanation: Six lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D2122C C06 to C08, D214A C07 to C09

names.official: Levy on electricity from solar radiation and tax on energy from renewable sources
names.native: Odvod z elektřiny ze slunečního záření; daň na energii z obnovitelných zdrojů

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: the solar levy (CZK 4.9 billion) and the tax on energy from renewable sources (CZK 22.5 billion, a line that did not exist in 2023).

instruments.explanation: The new line is the largest change among the Czech product taxes in 2024.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D214A C10 and C11

names.official: Levy on proceeds of lotteries
names.native: Odvod výtěžku z provozování loterií

taxes.base: Proceeds of lotteries and similar games.

instruments.explanation: CZK 21.9 billion in 2024, up 18%.

names.official: Road tax
names.native: Silniční daň

taxes.base: Vehicles used for business.
taxes.payer: Owners of vehicles used for business.

rate.headline: By engine and vehicle size
details: From 2022 the road tax was effectively abolished for cars, buses and trucks up to 12 tons; it remains for heavier vehicles (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (review of 27 July 2026), not checked against the Financial Administration.

instruments.explanation: CZK 1.2 billion in 2024.

names.official: Charges for water and air pollution and for the disposal of end-of-life vehicles
names.native: Poplatky za znečišťování vod a ovzduší; autovraky

taxes.base: Discharge of waste water into surface waters (CZK 0.18 billion), air pollution (CZK 0.38 billion), and charges for collecting vehicle wrecks (CZK 0.06 billion).

rate.headline: Set by the environmental laws
details: The tax on emission permits (CZK 18.6 billion) is the sale of a right and is not counted.

instruments.explanation: Small charges.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D29F C01, C02, C04, D214D C02

names.official: Payments for withdrawing land from the agricultural land fund and forest land, and fees collected by the Wine Fund
names.native: Odvody za odnětí půdy ze zemědělského půdního fondu; poplatky vinařského fondu

taxes.base: Taking farmland and forest land out of use (CZK 1.2 billion in all) and the fees of the Wine Fund (CZK 0.03 billion).

rate.headline: Set by law
details: Eurostat books CZK 0.33 billion of the transaction taxes (D214C) with local government; the list does not say which lines.

instruments.explanation: Six lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D214C, D29A C02 C03 C05, D214I

names.official: Television and radio licence fees (households and businesses)
names.native: Televizní a rozhlasové poplatky

taxes.base: Households and businesses with a television or radio.

rate.headline: A fixed monthly fee per household

instruments.explanation: The fees that finance Czech Television and Czech Radio.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D59D C01, D29E C02

names.official: Contributions to the Financial Market Guarantee System, the Securities Dealers Fund, the Loss Prevention Fund and the Travel Agencies Fund
names.native: Příspěvky do Garančního systému finančních trhů a dalších fondů

taxes.base: Financial Market Guarantee System (CZK 4.2 billion, down from CZK 6.4 billion in 2023), Securities Dealers Fund (CZK 0.4 billion), loss prevention fund (CZK 1.0 billion) and travel agencies fund (CZK 0.02 billion).
taxes.payer: Financial institutions, securities dealers and travel agencies.

instruments.explanation: Compulsory contributions that the statisticians book as taxes on production.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D29H C02 to C05

names.official: Administrative fees, other tax revenue and packaging registration fees
names.native: Správní poplatky; ostatní daňové příjmy
names.common: Administrative fees and other tax revenue

taxes.base: Administrative fees booked among taxes on production (CZK 1.4 billion) and among other current taxes (CZK 1.4 billion), other tax revenue and packaging registration fees.

rate.headline: Set by the Administrative Fees Act
details: Eurostat books CZK 0.7 billion of the taxes on production under local government; the list does not say which part of these fees is local, so they are drawn here.

instruments.explanation: Fees for official services.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D29H C01 and C08, D59F C03 and C04, D29E C01

names.official: Real estate tax (buildings and land; businesses and households)
names.native: Daň z nemovitostí

taxes.base: Land and buildings. The list gives CZK 19.7 billion for businesses and CZK 3.3 billion for households.

rate.headline: A national base with a municipal coefficient
details: The revenue nearly doubled in 2024, from CZK 12.5 billion to CZK 23.0 billion; the list does not give the reason.

instruments.explanation: The main tax of the municipalities.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D29A C01, D59A C01

names.official: Corporate income tax for municipalities and for regions
names.native: Daň z příjmů právnických osob za obce a za kraje
names.common: Corporate tax for municipalities and regions

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: corporate income tax assigned to municipalities (CZK 10.7 billion) and regions (CZK 1.0 billion); the list gives no more detail.
taxes.payer: Companies, including the municipalities and regions themselves as taxpayers.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: Eurostat books CZK 11.7 billion of corporate income tax under local government (S.1313).

instruments.explanation: The only income tax that Eurostat places with local government; the shared personal income tax is booked centrally.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D51B C02 and C03

names.official: Local fees: spa and recreation stay, advertising, admission, vehicle registration, dogs, entry permits and building land appreciation
names.native: Místní poplatky

taxes.base: Spa or recreational stays (CZK 1.7 billion), advertising (CZK 0.2 billion), admission fees (CZK 0.09 billion), vehicle registration (CZK 0.4 billion), dogs (CZK 0.3 billion), permits to enter selected places (CZK 0.02 billion) and the fee for the appreciation of building land (CZK 0.02 billion).

instruments.explanation: Eight small lines placed with local government.

legalRefs.locator: sheet CZ, D214H C01 and C06, D214E, D214D C01, D59F C01 and C02, D29A C04, D91B
